proposals.title: Cryo-CLEM profile: require the procedure's 0.9 NA / 2.0 mm working-distance objective to reach the grid (coupled WD clearance + NA cone)
proposals.description: bio_cryo_fluorescence_vitrified only requires 'optical_access present', so every windowed cryostat passes the optical part; on the e1 grid it is REQUIREMENTS_MET on CCS-100/300S/400, CRX-4K/VF, THMS600 (LNP96), THMSEL600 and OptistatDry BLV. The cited procedure images vitrified grids through a Nikon CFI TU Plan Apo 100x/0.9 air objective (Nikon: WD 2.0 mm) on a Linkam CMS196v3 stage that was optimised for high-NA lenses (fluorescence up to NA 0.9). Under-specified physics (b): add the existing validated coupled model objective_working_distance_clearance as MANDATORY and optical_na_vs_f_number as non-mandatory, with the procedure's objective as parameters. Exact JSON to add to the profile: params += [{"name":"objective_working_distance","value":{"value":2000,"unit":"um"},"origin":"manufacturer_specification","description":"Working distance of the Nikon CFI TU Plan Apo EPI 100x/0.90 used by Last et al. (Nikon lists WD 2.0 mm); enter your own objective","evidence_ids":["ev_exp_0013","<new: Nikon CFI60-2 table record>"]}, {"name":"extra_spacer","value":{"value":0,"unit":"um"},"origin":"user_entered","description":"No cover slip or extra window between objective and grid is stated by Last et al.; add any you insert"}, {"name":"objective_na","value":{"value":"0.9","unit":"NA"},"origin":"experimental_observation","evidence_ids":["ev_exp_0013"]}]; coupled += [{"model":"objective_working_distance_clearance","mandatory":true,"rationale":"Last et al. image the vitrified grid with a 0.9 NA air objective (Nikon CFI TU Plan Apo 100x/0.9, WD 2.0 mm). The grid must lie within that working distance: WD_stage_min + spacer <= 2.0 mm. A stage whose window geometry needs a longer WD (THMS600: 4.8 mm) cannot focus this objective on the sample."}, {"model":"optical_na_vs_f_number","mandatory":false,"rationale":"Reports whether the stage's optical cone admits NA 0.9 (NA^2(4N^2+1) <= 1, i.e. N <= 0.242). Non-mandatory: a vignetted cone lowers collection efficiency but does not make imaging impossible."}]. The temperature (at_most 136 K), optical_access and frost requirements are unchanged.
proposals.validity: Air between objective and window (n = 1); working distances measured along the same optical axis; s_spacer = any cover slip or extra window the user adds; NA cone uses the thin-lens relation tan(theta) = 1/(2N) (existing model optical_na_vs_f_number, validity 0 <= NA <= 1). Valid for the procedure's 100x/0.9 objective; a user with a long-WD, lower-NA objective edits objective_working_distance/objective_na (the edit resets confirmation).

proposals.title: Cryo-CLEM profile: require cold, dry loading of the vitrified grid (new flag key sample.cryo_transfer)
proposals.description: The profile checks only that the stage can get below 136 K. Vitrified grids must stay below the devitrification temperature and away from humid air from plunge-freezing to imaging, so the grid has to be loaded into a pre-cooled, dry stage (LN2 cassette/shuttle into a pre-cooled loading chamber). Sample-in-vacuum cryostats and probe stations are loaded warm, then pumped and cooled (CRX-VF cycle: 1.5 h pump-down, 5 h cooldown, 2 h warm-up), which would devitrify the specimen. Under-specified physics (b). Exact JSON: vocabulary += {"sample.cryo_transfer":{"shape":"flag","unit":"","description":"A vitrified/frozen specimen can be loaded into the pre-cooled sample position and kept below its devitrification temperature and away from humid air during loading (e.g. LN2-cooled transfer cassette or shuttle into a pre-cooled dry loading chamber)","status":"established","better":"flag"}}; requirements += {"key":"sample.cryo_transfer","constraint":{"kind":"present"},"mandatory":true,"origin":"experimental_observation","rationale":"Vitrified grids must be kept below ~136 K (Last et al.) and dry during transfer and imaging (Schorb et al. 2017); the cryo-stage must be pre-cooled before the sample is inserted (Kaufmann et al. 2014). The procedure's stage (Linkam CMS196) loads a grid cassette from a sealed container into a pre-cooled dry loading chamber. A stage that must be loaded warm and then cooled cannot keep the specimen vitrified.","evidence_ids":["ev_exp_0009","ev_exp_0017","ev_exp_0018","<new: Schorb 2017, Kaufmann 2014, Linkam CMS196 records>"]}.
proposals.validity: Applies to vitrified (plunge-frozen or high-pressure-frozen) specimens, which is this profile's scope; not to samples that tolerate warm loading. The literature threshold ranges from ~135 K (Kaufmann et al.) to -140 C / 133 K (Schorb & Briggs; Linkam) and ~136 K (Last et al.).

proposals.expected_effect: Alone (Lean-checked, e1 database): bio_cryo_fluorescence_vitrified MET 8/NOT 3/NEED 15 -> MET 0/NOT 3/NEED 23 (all eight MET -> NEED INFO). Together with R1: MET 0/NOT 6/NEED 20 (no further change; THMS600 stays NOT MET on the WD clearance). Latest seeds alone: 10/11/5 -> 0/11/15. Once the data workflow records sample.cryo_transfer = false (trusted) for warm-loaded cryostats, those pairs become NOT MET; a cryo-CLEM stage such as the CMS196 would be the only route to MET.

proposals.title: Photoluminescence profile: drop the 25 x 25 mm sample-size requirement that the cited cryostat measurements never used; record the transmission geometry
proposals.description: Wrong number (c). chem_temperature_dependent_photoluminescence requires sample.width.max >= 25 mm and sample.length.max >= 25 mm because 'Swidinsky et al. used 25 x 25 x 2 mm fused silica substrates mounted on the coldfinger'. In the paper the fused-silica substrates were used only for room-temperature absorbance and same-side spectra outside the cryostat; every cryostat measurement (emission spectra at 300/87/4 K, time-resolved data at 18 temperatures) used 5 mm acrylic substrates 'machined to fit the dimensions necessary for the cryochamber', whose lateral size is not stated. The sample size was set by the cryostat, not the other way round, so no sample-size requirement follows from the procedure. Geometry (as requested): the cryostat sample faces the side windows on the cold finger, i.e. it is inserted end-on (plate plane contains the cryostat axis); a bore-based fit would need W^2 + t^2 <= D^2, but W is unknown, and replacing the width/length keys by sample.bore_diameter would not be physically equivalent because holders are narrower than bores (OptistatDry BLV: holder 20 x 50 mm in a 40 x 50 mm sample space). proposals.risks: Low impact today; the mK profile mixes a dc-transport and an RF procedure, so optional items are only a stopgap.

rejected_ideas: keys alternative sample.bore_diameter (or sample.diameter.max) for the 3 x 3 x 3 mm crystal in mat_electrical_resistance_low_temperature / mat_magnetoresistance_10T: not physically equivalent. The crystal lies across the bore on the PPMS puck, a '2.3 cm (0.91 inch) diameter disk' inside a 'Clear bore 2.5 cm (1 inch) diameter'; the ETO/Resistivity manuals give no mounting-area figure, so the bore is only a necessary bound (a 4.24 mm footprint diagonal never binds). The project rule also forbids relaxing the 3 mm requirement to reach MET.

keys alternative sample.bore_diameter for the 15 mm Raman crucible: not equivalent. The liquid-filled crucible must lie flat and be viewed from above on the stage's sample area (THMS600 'Sample area 22 mm diameter'); in side-window cryostats the holder is narrower than the bore (OptistatDry BLV holder 20 x 50 mm in a 40 x 50 mm space).

Making the transmon chip-size requirements (7 x 7 mm, Place et al.) non-mandatory because the chip sits in a user package: rejected. Bluefors sells the QCage.24 holder 'tested and pre-installed' at the mixing-chamber flange of LD systems, so the chip limit can be a configuration capability like the PPMS puck; keep the requirement and document the installed holder's chip size.

Necessary-only bore checks as extra coupled constraints (across the bore W^2 + L^2 <= D^2, end-on W^2 + t^2 <= D^2): sound as necessary conditions, but none binds for the current profiles (3 mm crystal, 15 mm crucible; the PL sample size is unstated after R4), so no verdict value now.

Allowing module.dc_resistivity as an alternative to module.electrical_transport in the transport profiles: Nowakowska et al. measured 'with ac electrical current flowing along [100]', and Quantum Design describes the ETO as AC resistance and the Resistivity Option as DC resistance, so the alternative is not the procedure's measurement.

Raising mat_magnetoresistance_10T to 14 T: Nowakowska et al.'s SdH analysis uses B_eff 'obtained for B1 = 14 T and B2 = 9 T', so 10 T would not reproduce it; but 10 T is the user's documented demo value (origin user_entered), so it is kept and only flagged here.

Illumination-heating coupled model T_stage + dT(P) <= 136 K for cryo-fluorescence: Last et al. give power-density limits per grid type measured with the stage at 77 K, not temperature rises in K, and Huebinger & Bastiaens report 'a new steady-state temperature between -108 C and -115 C, depending on beam shape' at ~300 W/cm2; the heating is a grid/illumination property, every catalog stage reaches <= 78 K, so there is no verdict effect.
Tightening the devitrification limit from 136 K to 133 K (-140 C per Linkam and Schorb & Briggs): no verdict effect; the procedure's own value (Last et al., ~136 K) is kept.

Requiring a dry-gas purge instead of vacuum for the open aqueous Raman sample (an evacuated sample space would evaporate the liquid): physically plausible, but Park et al. do not describe the stage atmosphere and a sealed cell would be compatible with vacuum; R3 already removes the probe-station acceptances.

Requiring a transmitted-light path (>= 2 windows) for polarized optical microscopy: the wax procedure states only a 'Leica DM2700 polarized optical microscope with an Olympus long-distance lens', not transmitted light; the long-distance lens's working distance is not stated either, so no WD requirement can be set.

Raising the transmon coax bandwidth from 8 GHz to >= 10.5 GHz for Tuokkola et al.'s TWPA pump: the TWPA is optional in the procedure (unpumped in the first cooldown; 'the TWPA does not significantly affect the coherence times'), so the 8 GHz margin above the 7.3 GHz resonators is kept.

Inert-atmosphere requirement for the air-sensitive REBi crystals ('oxidize easily in ambient atmosphere and decompose after several hours'): needs a new key; the PPMS chamber always holds helium exchange gas, while [vacuum.available, purge.gas] would give spurious failures for the classic PPMS; no verdict value.

keys alternatives [temperature.range, temperature.base] for the quantum temperature requirements: Lean-checked, zero verdict change, because combineAny returns unknown when one alternative is missing; replaced by R6.

Accepting the cryochamber range as an alternative to the specimen-head range in bio_cryosection_frozen_tissue: not equivalent. Li et al. set the holder 2 C warmer than the chamber (-18 C vs -20 C), which needs active object-head control; without it the specimen equilibrates near the chamber temperature, so leica_cm1950_genA_standard (object cooling not installed) is correctly NOT MET for this procedure.

Schema note instead of a requirement: sample.height.max mixes sample thickness (Linkam THMS600 'Maximum Sample Thickness: 3mm', ev_linkam_0013) and vertical sample-space height (OptistatDry BLV '40 mm x 50 mm'); a thickness requirement (e.g. the 5 mm PL acrylic) would be checked against unlike quantities. Proposed for the data/schema workflow: split into sample.thickness.max and sample_space.height.
